article.summary: distill-kura is a local-first, file-based long-term memory service for agents. It stores one Markdown file per memory and a recognition-oriented index, gates transcript distillation with deterministic evidence checks, and retrieves relevant memories through a fast direct-match path or model-assisted selection followed by link walking.

who_what.text: The catalog places distill-kura at ordinal 192, uses slug distill-kura, and lists the explicit locator https://github.com/lna-lab/distill-kura. Its pinned Atlas report is retained only for identity and locator attribution.

The official public repository is https://github.com/lna-lab/distill-kura; the GitHub repository page identifies master as the default branch. The official master Atom feed identifies full head 3a02c04e5155cd66d49cfd95d11b09239499c97d and was updated at 2026-09-30T10:40:08Z.

The README describes a Python file-based memory package, shipped with a DeepSeek Harness plugin, MCP bridge, HTTP service, CLI, and Python library. It describes the system as standard-library-only with no vector database or embedding dependency.
The official pinned README was checked for a published contact email and none was found. No commit/profile metadata or third-party directories were used.

architecture.text: A store is a directory containing MEMORY.md, one Markdown file per memory, optional _study notes, and a private _still work area for drafts, watermarks, read logs, write-ahead records, and revision state. The implementation uses deterministic file operations; the thinker model is used for semantic index selection when the fast path has no confident hit.

Memory frontmatter includes a slug/name, description, type and optional tags plus curation annotations; body prose carries the remembered fact, rationale, application guidance, and [[slug]] relations. The index contains one recognition trigger per memory and supports structured sections and derived links. There is no vector database or embedding store in the described design.

Distillation separates intake, candidate generation, a deterministic gate, novelty checks, composition, draft staging, and a later cold re-read that pours, fixes, or discards each draft. Evidence manifests and signed draft envelopes support verification before canonical store mutation.

The store's doctor report exposes health and integrity information including dead links, isolated memories, index drift, evidence-manifest problems, revision/WAL replay state, hardlinks, curation marks, retired entries, fastpath state, and observed capacity units.

behavior.text: Write by distillation: journal adapters classify transcript segments as USER, TOOL, ACT, or SELF. The brain proposes memory candidates with quotes; the gate accepts only surviving quotes found verbatim in the matching class material, suppresses quotes already present in the store, requires self-only material to be framed as judgement, and flags numbers without TOOL/ACT support. Later model-written surfaces are rechecked for unsupported numbers, attribution, links, and quotations.

Draft lifecycle: model output is staged rather than immediately becoming memory. The scribe re-reads each draft without its earlier context and chooses pour, fix, or toss; failures and pending intake are retained for retry rather than silently treated as empty work. Direct remember and annotation routes are separately controlled by the store's write_policy.

Update/correction: ordinary annotation merges tags and curation text onto a memory; a dedicated retirement operation changes the index line to show a superseded memory and successor. Retirement requires an evidence manifest whose single USER-class quote explicitly names the old memory, states a replacement/retirement construction, and names its successor. It does not erase the old Markdown memory.

Delete: no general memory deletion or secure-erasure route is described in the inspected API/docs. Retirement is a marked transition, and retired memories remain stored and can remain in the index/retrieval path. Backup, filesystem, and model-retention behavior is outside the in-process operation.

Retrieval: a deterministic fastpath tries direct recognition and only returns gated hits; otherwise a thinker receives the full recognition index and names relevant slugs by meaning. The store walks links from those picks and returns context subject to per-memory and whole-context character limits. If the thinker is unavailable, recall falls back to index-line word overlap and labels the degraded method; an explicit empty model selection remains an abstention.

Scope: each store is a separate directory, with modes/session configuration selecting the store before a conversation. Directories and mode binding are routing boundaries, not authorization: the HTTP server has no authentication. Trust documentation calls for process/user and filesystem separation, warns that hardlinked files are served, and notes that shared models or journal roots can cross intended privacy boundaries.

Provenance: the deterministic gate verifies that quoted text occurs in a classified raw source and that claims follow the surviving evidence classes; manifests preserve evidence references, and retirement re-proves the transition from a USER quote. This establishes traceability to source text/classification, not the truth of a statement or correctness of the journal adapter's classification. The trust docs also identify filesystem access to adjacent gate keys/manifests as outside the threat boundary.

Efficiency and observability: source design avoids embeddings and a vector database; direct recognition can bypass a thinker call, while meaning-based selection sends the index to a model. Recall reports method, fastpath verdict/time, walked and included slugs, budget drops, estimated tokens, and elapsed time. The README and store doctor describe JSONL distillation metrics/logs and store-health/integrity counters; these are observability surfaces, not measurements from this review.

metrics.evidence: The gate checks source-text occurrence and class rules; no response claim adjudication was performed.
Recall includes timing fields, but no timing samples were collected in this review.
No acknowledged writes or scheduled recall probes were run.
The code can report estimated context tokens, but no provider usage or cost accounting was collected.
Doctor exposes memory/index/body estimates and bytes, but no benchmark corpus footprint was measured.

limits.text: The evidence gate verifies quote occurrence and permitted claim forms, not that the source is truthful, complete, or correctly classified; a contaminated journal or misclassified source can still ground a memory in the wrong way.

The retrieval meaning tier depends on the configured model; degraded word-overlap recall and direct fastpath cover different query shapes. Source design does not establish recall accuracy for a workload.

Store/mode selection is not confidentiality enforcement. An unauthenticated HTTP endpoint, shared model/journal configuration, filesystem access, or hardlinks can expose content outside the intended mode boundary.
Retirement records a supersession face but preserves the old memory. The inspected material does not establish hard deletion, backup erasure, hosted-model retention, or comprehensive secure erasure.
No distill-kura runtime, tests, or benchmark workloads were run for this review. All project metric domains remain unmeasured.
